claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Adding 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr binder and using SPS at 1500 °C enables ZrB2 densification at a lower temperature than conventional single-phase ZrB2 processing.
The 30% AlFeNiCoCr binder combined with SPS at 1500 °C reduces residual porosity in the ZrB2 cermet.
The intervention reduces the formation of channels that permit molten-aluminum penetration.
At 1500 °C, the AlFeNiCoCr binder becomes sufficiently fluid to fill intergranular pores uniformly.
The fluid binder creates strong interparticle connections between ZrB2 grains.
Binder-assisted pore filling and grain bonding increase densification.
Binder-assisted pore filling and grain bonding improve mechanical properties.
A compact, low-porosity microstructure minimizes pathways for molten aluminum infiltration.
Reduced molten-aluminum infiltration lowers corrosion and subsequent component failure during liquid-bath exposure.
The 1500 °C cermet will have a relative density near 97.7%.
The 1500 °C cermet will have higher relative density than both conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 and otherwise identical cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The 1500 °C cermet will exhibit improved hardness compared with the stated controls.
The 1500 °C cermet will exhibit fracture toughness exceeding the cited pure-ZrB2 reference value of 4.5 MPa·m^1/2.
The 1500 °C cermet will exhibit lower molten-aluminum corrosion rates than the stated controls.
The 1500 °C cermet will exhibit lower wear volume than the stated controls.
The proposed preparation uses SPS at 1500 °C, 50 MPa, approximately 200 °C/min, under vacuum, with a 5-minute dwell.
The stated service boundary is molten-aluminum immersion at 700 °C for up to 12 days.
Changing binder content, SPS schedule, or service environment could alter performance.
